correctness.rationale: Complete direct graph enumeration with explicit 36-edge input: no dominating 6/7-set in 480,700 candidates; 1,767 dominating 8-sets; every one of 58,905 four-edge deletion sets preserves at least 5 such sets; precisely 276 of all 376,992 five-edge deletion sets destroy all. Every one has a complete vertex star, exactly 36 have two; 48 adjacency-preserving bijections produce eight disjoint orbits. Explicit nine-vertex dominators checked for each orbit imply post-deletion domination number nine throughout. Separate critical-edge-bundle implementation agrees on all 276 sets. Fully finite conclusion: no extrapolation.

evidence: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.02477v1 gives b(T)=5; its Section 4 checks every four-edge set and one five-edge witness.
The general planar bounds and the 1990 bondage-number definition concern minimal deletion cardinality rather than enumeration of all minimizers.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Knowing a minimum cardinality and finding one witness is strictly weaker than enumerating all 276 labeled minimizing edge subsets and their automorphism orbits. No reviewed dominating theorem or exact stronger parameter was found that implies this census.

value.rationale: Complete critical-fault profile of the published cubic planar counterexample to the planar bondage conjecture: enumerates every minimum destructive five-edge set rather than one witness, shows unavoidable three-edge incident star, 13 local extensions per vertex, 36 double-star cases, and an eight-orbit decomposition. A natural extremal graph/invariant pairing with structural significance for sensitivity of domination to optimal edge failures, not an arbitrary induced subgraph slice.
